01. Each open position has specific attachment requirements in order to be considered by the hiring committee. If the attachment directions are not followed, your application will not be considered. The required attachments for this position are: • Cover letter (see instructions in Additional Information section); • Resume; • Professional Reference List (see instructions in Additional Information section); • Diversity Statement. (See further document instructions below); • A current Athletic Trainer Certificate (ATC) from the National Athletic Trainers' Association Board of Certification (NATABOC); and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and Automatic External Defibrillator (AED) for the Professional Rescuer.; • Unofficial Transcripts (see instructions in Additional Information section); Have you attached the correct required documents to your application? Options: Yes | No
Provide advanced first aid and therapeutic techniques and refer to a physician or appropriate medical facility if deemed necessary;
Advanced principles and practices of first aid, CPR, physiology, anatomy, and kinesiology;
Valid driver's license and eligible to obtain California driver's license upon hire;
Administer first aid and emergency medical care including lifesaving procedures to student athletes;
Operation of a variety of first aid, and therapeutic equipment;
A current Athletic Trainer Certificate (ATC) from the National Athletic Trainers' Association Board of Certification (NATABOC); and
Conduct body composition analysis and urinalysis testing for wrestling weight certification;
Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and Automatic External Defibrillator (AED) for the Professional Rescuer.
Two years of experience as a college athletic trainer. A graduate degree in a relevant field may substitute for the two years.
Five years of experience as a college athletic trainer. A graduate degree in a relevant field may substitute for two of the years.
Supervise and instruct athletic training students and oversee their education and field experience;
Provide athletic training services to student athletes engaged in traditional and non-traditional seasons of intercollegiate athletics;
Principles, practices, procedures, techniques, and equipment used in the prevention, care, and rehabilitation of athletic injuries;
Work a flexible schedule according to the season of sport. Work hours will generally be Monday – Friday 10-6:30;
Evaluate and diagnose student athletes' injuries;
Practices, procedures and techniques involved in taping, stretching, and wrapping athletes to prevent injury or re-injury;
Work some evening and weekend hours depending of the needs of the department;
Provide proper rehabilitation and reconditioning based on the diagnosis and/or in accordance with physician instruction;
Recognition and evaluation of athletic injuries;
Perform duties in multiple environments. Environments may include, but are not limited to gymnasiums, athletics fields and pool decks;
Attend and provide athletic training and risk management services for home sporting events as assigned;
Appropriate situations for physician referral;
Establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with those contacted in the performance of duties; and
Provide care for both the home and visiting teams;
Principles in counseling students with personal health issues;

Demonstrate a sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, and ethnic backgrounds of staff and students and of staff and students with physical and learning disabilities.
Advise and counsel athletes and coaches in the development of physical conditioning and training programs to enhance athlete strength, endurance, flexibility and coordination;
Physical fitness, hygiene, disinfectant, and safety procedures related to athletics;
Lift, carry, push, and/or pull up to 50 pounds;
Meet with teams to review and assist with health screening examinations and other required medical forms prior to participation in athletics in coordination with the requirements of the CCCAA;
Proper techniques to prevent personal injury in carrying out physical requirements of the position;
Read and comprehend printed matter and text and data on computer monitors;
Complete and process paperwork such as: pre-participation medical packet, emergency and daily treatment reports, detailed injury reports, insurance claim forms, and doctor notes/releases;
Detail oriented record-keeping techniques;
Sit or stand for extended periods of time; and
Maintain the athletic training room by keeping all sinks, baths, tables and other modalities organized, sanitary and in proper working order;
Current technologies, personal computer, and associated office software such as word processing, spreadsheet, presentation, and/or database software; and
Exert manual dexterity sufficient for keyboard and other office equipment operation.
Administer technical directions issued by physicians;
CCCAA Constitution and Bylaws.
Promote and maintain a professional environment for the treatment of both sexes; and
Perform other related duties as required.
Collaborate and assist the Athletic Trainer for the above essential functions;
Aid with organization and implementation of concussion management system in accordance with governing bodies;
Assist with inventory and equipment needs, requisitions and organize supplies;
Assist with scheduling the work of athletic training students;
Monitor athletic training students in accordance with the protocol established by the Athletic Trainer; and
Assist with scheduling physicians for athletic training room clinics.
Oversee organization and implementation of concussion management system in accordance with governing bodies;
Conduct bi-annual concussion education meetings with athletes and coaches in accordance with governing bodies;
Organize and implement bi-annual concussion baseline testing in accordance with governing bodies;
Act in a lead capacity to oversee and mentor the Assistant Athletic Trainer;
Assign and coordinate the work delegated to the Assistant Athletic Trainer;
Prepare written policies and procedures in collaboration with the college policy regarding emergency management;
Oversee, research, and analyze inventory and equipment needs;
Oversee completion of requisitions and organization of supplies;
Develops, directs policies and procedures for athletic training room and athletic training students;
Oversee and schedule the work of athletic training students;
Complete and process paperwork for independent study students and volunteer workers;
Conduct informational meetings annually on Blood-borne Pathogens as required by Board policy;
Develop a plan to accommodate Athletic Trainer services and home athletic contests within the available budget;
Oversee scheduling physicians for athletic training room clinics;
Schedule meetings with the Athletic Director to review and update CCCAA and college medical policies;
Submit, in accordance with CCCAA guidelines, appropriate medical documentation required for injury illness waiver requests which impacts student athlete eligibility;
Work in collaboration with the students' insurance agent, reviews athletic insurance coverage and assists student athletes and staff in the correct submission of insurance claims; and
Organize meetings with Health Center Coordinator to review student-athlete and college insurance policies.
Provide medical and athletic training services to the students registered in the Advanced Skill and Training Development classes;
Liability issues that confront the modern athletic program;
Communicate intelligibly and effectively via speech, telephone, written correspondence, and/or email;
In the absence of the team physician, advise coaches and athletes on the ability of the injured athlete to participate;
Adhere to Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) compliance guidelines;
Operate a wide variety of therapeutic and rehabilitative equipment;
